security_spec.violation_condition: In the Linux kernel, when the SBI SSE handler dispatches event_id 0xffff0001 (local unknown NMI) and the kernel either (a) lacks a registered handler, leaving the event unacknowledged and permanently blocking lower-priority SSE events on that hart, or (b) the handler fails to save/restore the full interrupted context (sepc, sstatus.SPP/SPIE/SDT, A6) before invoking generic NMI handling, or (c) the handler fails to call sbi_sse_complete, stranding the event in RUNNING state and breaking the SSE state machine for all local events on that hart.
security_spec.summary: Kernel must handle local unknown NMI SSE event (0xffff0001) to completion; failure to register, save full interrupted context, or call sbi_sse_complete strands the event in RUNNING state, permanently blocking all lower-priority SSE events on the affected hart

findings.finding: The SBI SSE (Supervisor Software Events) extension ID (0x535345) is not defined in sbi.h. No sbi_sse_complete, sbi_sse_event_handler, or any SSE-related SBI function IDs exist. The kernel has zero infrastructure for registering, dispatching, or completing SSE events. The only SSE-related definition is SBI_MPXY_ATTR_SSE_EVENT_ID (line 467), which is an MPXY channel attribute for associating a channel with an SSE event — not an SSE handler itself.

spec_citations.excerpt: Supervisor Software Events (SSE), an extension to the SBI, provide a mechanism for supervisor software to register and service system events emanating from an SBI implementation, such as firmware or a hypervisor.

findings.finding: No handler for SSE event 0xffff0001 (local unknown NMI) exists anywhere in the kernel. The traps.c NMI handling paths (DO_ERROR_INFO for illegal instructions, breakpoints, etc.) are CSRs-triggered NMIs from machine-mode hardware traps, not SBI SSE software-injected events. There is no code path that would save/restore the full interrupted context (sepc, sstatus.SPP/SPIE/SDT, A6) followed by sbi_sse_complete(), because the SSE extension is entirely unimplemented.

findings.finding: The MPXY mailbox driver reads sse_event_id as a channel attribute but never registers an SSE event handler for it. If firmware delivers SSE events (including event 0xffff0001) via MPXY channels with SSE capability (SBI_MPXY_CHAN_CAP_SSE), the kernel has no handler to acknowledge or complete these events. This could strand the SSE event in RUNNING state on the firing hart, blocking lower-priority events.
